paper.title: Spontaneous regression of a metastatic melanoma pulmonary deposit following biopsy
paper.abstract:
Spontaneous complete and partial regression of metastatic melanoma is poorly under-
stood, and is a rare phenomenon with less than 80 cases reported since 1866. Several
correlations have been noted such as systemic or local infections, operative trauma, hor-
monal inﬂuences, nutrition and immunologic factors. We present FDG PET and CT ﬁndings
in a patient with multiple pulmonary metastases of melanoma, one of which underwent
regression following biopsy. We suggest immune system modulation, triggered by biopsy,
could have played a role, although the precise mechanism remains unknown.

evidence_refs.quote:
Spontaneous complete and partial regression of metastatic melanoma is poorly under-
stood, and is a rare phenomenon with less than 80 cases reported since 1866. Several
correlations have been noted such as systemic or local infections, operative trauma, hor-
monal inﬂuences, nutrition and immunologic factors. We present FDG PET and CT ﬁndings
in a patient with multiple pulmonary metastases of melanoma, one of which underwent
regression following biopsy. We suggest immune system modulation, triggered by biopsy,
could have played a role, although the precise mechanism remains unknown.
Case Report
A CT-guided biopsy of the left lower lobe nodule was positive for metastatic melanoma.
On the other hand, the previously biopsied left lung nodule has decreased in size and showed very minimal FDG uptake with max SUV of 2.5
The left lower lobe nodule (A) has decreased to 17 × 14 mm in size.
Interestingly, despite the recurrence of disease, the biopsied lesion continued to decrease in size throughout the 19 months that followed after initial diagnosis.
A 55-year-old woman presented with night sweats, cough, and hemoptysis.
A 55-year-old woman presented with night sweats, cough, and hemoptysis.
A CT-guided biopsy of the left lower lobe nodule was positive for metastatic melanoma.
Patient had no history of melanoma and clinical examination did not reveal a primary lesion.
In addition to the left lower lobe pulmonary nodule, smaller cavitary lesions were seen in the bilateral upper lungs (Fig. 2).
Note left hilar nodal spread (arrowhead).
Unfortunately, as is common with this form of treatment, melanoma recurred with lung, brain, and spinal cord metastases, this time resistant to ipilimumab.
Fig. 3 – Positron emission tomography–computed tomography images, 43 days later. The left lower lobe nodule (A) has decreased to 17 × 14 mm in size.
